title: SQL Joins

content.intro: In this lesson, you will study sql joins in the context of sql, databases, and data management. You will connect the PDF subtopics to a small example and practice describing what the evidence does—and does not—support.
content.why_it_matters: SQL Joins matters because it affects how data is collected, represented, analyzed, interpreted, or used in a decision. Check the task and assumptions before choosing a method.

content_blocks.title: The central idea
content_blocks.text: SQL is a declarative language for querying and transforming relational data. Correct join keys, null semantics, and transaction boundaries matter as much as query syntax.

content_blocks.title: Guided walkthrough
content_blocks.text: 1. Restate the question addressed by sql joins. 2. Identify the input data, intended output, and assumptions. 3. Predict what the small example should show before reading its output. 4. Change one input or assumption, compare the result, and document what remains uncertain.

content_blocks.code:
SELECT category, SUM(amount) AS revenue
FROM orders
GROUP BY category
ORDER BY revenue DESC;
content_blocks.expected_output: Query simulation: one result row per category; sorted by revenue descending.

For SQL, adapt the query to an approved local schema; the stated result is a conceptual query simulation, not a live database result.
content_blocks.reset_steps: Restore the provided synthetic input, rerun or retrace the example, and change one value at a time. Do not use personal records, credentials, or data you are not authorized to access.

content_blocks.title: Common mistakes and fixes
content_blocks.text: Keep the question, data grain, units, and assumptions explicit. If a result differs, inspect the input and steps in order. Avoid turning an observed association into a causal claim, treating a sample as the population, or assuming a small demonstration guarantees production behavior. SQL is shown for inspection. Run it only against a local or approved database schema.

content_blocks.title: Responsible interpretation
content_blocks.text: This example is a teaching aid. It is static in the CodeLeaf lesson and is not executed in the browser. It uses small synthetic values; validate any real workflow in a separate, appropriate local environment and protect sensitive data.
